children: Broadcom Inc. (NASDAQ:AVGO) reported a blowout Q3—$29.6B revenue, $13.09B GAAP net, $3.32 non‑GAAP EPS and $16.7B in AI chip sales—while naming Anthropic its top XPU customer, raising Q4 AI guidance and drawing bullish analyst targets and ARK Invest buys as it cements its AI inference leadership.
: Broadcom (AVGO) Q3: revenue $29.6B (+86% y/y), GAAP net income $13.09B, non‑GAAP EPS $3.32, AI chip revenue $16.7B (+221%), FCF ~$13.7B. Q4 rev guide ~$34.8B; AI guide $21.7B.
: Broadcom (AVGO) says Anthropic is becoming its top XPU customer and OpenAI second, pushing Alphabet to third; company also reports stronger ties with Alphabet’s TPU business and AI customer growth.
: Analysts updated Broadcom (AVGO) targets: Citigroup $515, Cantor Fitzgerald $600, Evercore $578, KeyBanc $575, RBC $400; Morgan Stanley and BMO kept bullish ratings.

: Broadcom Inc. (AVGO) is highlighted as a leading AI inference play; its custom chips target high-volume, repetitive inference workloads and benefit from AI spending shifting to application inference.
: ARK Invest bought 55,131 Broadcom (AVGO) shares (~$20.5M) across three ETFs ahead of AVGO’s fiscal Q3 earnings release on Sept. 2, after adding to its AVGO position earlier that week.
